concept.title: Topicmap Signs and Represented Objects
concept.shortdesc: The sign you press on, the Topic that the Topicmap projection holds for it, the TMDM object that Topic represents and the Lisp objects the projection was derived from are five different things. Inspect Topicmap sign opens the projected Topic; Inspect represented object opens the TMDM object it represents.

section.title: Five things
section.p: The Topicmap of an Item edit is drawn from a Topic Map that the topic-maps reader makes of a CTM text. The CTM text is derived from the Lisp objects of the Item edit. Between the Lisp objects and the pixels there are five distinct things, and the two inspection Operations of the marking menu (see Topicmap Gesture Operations) reach two of them.

dlentry.dt: Browser SVG sign, a concrete gesture occurrence
dlentry.dd: One SVG element drawn for one Topic in one pane. In the native Topicmap it is the transparent rectangle of class dreyeck-topicmap-workspace-action over the Topic; in TALA (interactive) it is the group g of the Topic. Gesture input is bound to this element. An occurrence (workspace-action-sign-occurrence) records the Topic, the projection, the Workspace if there is one, the pane and the element. A refresh replaces the element and the occurrence ends with it; the same Topic drawn again is a new occurrence.

A topicmap-projection: the Topics and Associations that the renderers draw, with their positions and visibility. It is derived from the Lisp objects each time a view is shown; current-projection keeps the last one of an origin object while its CTM text is unchanged, so that the Workspace Point survives a refresh.

An item-edit-topic. It has an id (its key in the Topic Map), a label, view properties, the TMDM object it represents, and its origin, the CTM of the Item edit. It also carries the provenance: it is an object of the Item edit, an Association of the Item edit, or a schema Topic.
What topicmap-topic-object-of returns for the projected Topic: a TMDM Topic (topic) or a TMDM Association (association) of the Topic Map that the topic-maps reader made.

The objects the CTM text is derived from: the edit proposal, the preview or the completion, the Story Item as observed, the Action. project-item-edit reads them and changes nothing. The projection keeps for every Topic which Lisp object it came from and how that is known, observed or derived. That provenance is part of the HyperDoc projection and is not stated in the Topic Map.

section.title: Example: the Association node proposes
section.p: The example is the edit proposal for the Item E3 (ed37e9bac2fcd548) of the page ctm-and-tmdm-in-hyperdoc. The Topicmap of a completion draws the same node among more objects. The references below open the objects of the proposal that the Catalog prepares from that page file; preparing it writes nothing, and a Catalog that does not serve that page answers with an explanation instead.

ol.li: The Association proposes is drawn as a node of its own, with the id proposes(action=the-proposed-action,proposal=the-proposal). Two edges join it to its players, one for each Role. The proposal itself is the proposal and the Topicmap is made from its CTM.

Inspect Topicmap sign on the node opens the projected Topic proposes, an item-edit-topic. Its Provenance view says that it is an Association of the Item edit, known as derived, because the function proposal-action makes the Action from the proposal now and the proposal holds none.
Inspect represented object on the same node opens the TMDM Association proposes that the projected Topic represents: a TMDM Association of type proposes with the Scope derived and two Roles.
From the projected Topic, the Provenance table links the Lisp objects: the proposal as player of the Role proposal and the proposed Action as player of the Role action.

section.title: Why the projected Topic and the TMDM object are not the same

ul.li: They are objects of different classes with different content. The projected Topic holds the provenance, the position and the visibility; the TMDM Association holds its type, its Scope and its Roles and nothing else. The reason why HyperDoc states the Association as derived is kept in the projection; the Topic Map carries only the class as the Scope.
They have different lifetimes. The projection is made again when a view is shown, and the Topic Map is read from the CTM text; an equal CTM text gives a new Topic Map object.

They are joined by one link: the projected Topic holds the TMDM object and reports it as topicmap-topic-object-of. Inspect Topicmap sign ends at the projected Topic; Inspect represented object follows that link and ends at the other side of it.

The key of the projected Topic is not an identifier of the TMDM object. For an Association node it is made from the type and the Roles, type(role=player,...), so that two reads of one CTM text give the same key.
